title: Failure to re-render old tutorials
description:
**TLDR**: 
- **_the problem_: tutorial fails to render with obscure error**
- **_the quick fix_: delete old .html file and re-run tutorial**

## The problem

In a nutshell, the problem is trying to re-render an unchanged old tutorial with updated versions of `rmarkdown` and `learnr`, while still preserving the old .html artifact from a previous run. Here's step-by-step workflow that is unfortunately likely to result in an obscure error. If you:

1. have a `learnr` tutorial (or any `runtime: shiny_prerendered` .Rmd document) **AND**
2. had previously run that .Rmd document **AND** 
3. preserved the .html artifact **AND**
4. recently updated the `learnr` and `rmarkdown` packages **AND**
5. tried to re-run the .Rmd without any changes **AND**
6. encountered an obscure error involving failing to normalize a path...

... then, this issue is for you. This is fairly common and even encouraged workflow for tutorial authors, so it's regrettable that such a common workflow could cause such an obscure error. We've improved the error message in the development version of Shiny (version > 1.0.5), but this is still far from ideal.

Here's what you may see for Shiny version 1.0.5 (or lower), both in the R Markdown console, and in the viewer/window (i.e. where the tutorial or app usually appears):

```sh
Warning: Error in normalizePath: path[1]="": No such file or directory    # in Rmd console
ERROR: path[1]="": No such file or directory                              # in app viewer
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6527540/37715966-49db59d2-2d15-11e8-8217-f26f88a1a645.png)

And here's what you may see for Shiny version greater than 1.0.5 (currently only available from github: `devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny")`) -- in this case, both the R Markdown console and the viewer give the same, slightly more descriptive error:

```sh
ERROR: Couldn't normalize path in `addResourcePath`, with arguments: 
  `prefix` = 'highlightjs-1.1'; `directoryPath` = ''
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6527540/37715933-2f6b1dbc-2d15-11e8-9cbf-5844f9a476ab.png)

## The quick fix
The very high-level reason for this bug is that the old .html file cached some now out-of-date dependencies, which the current version of `rmarkdown` tries to load, but fails to. For more details on this, see the next section. For this section, we only care about the fact that this problem is caused by the old .html file generated by a previous run. This means that:

- deleting the .html file **OR**
- moving the .html file to another directory **OR** 
- even just changing the .Rmd document (so as to force it to knit again) 

**AND** then running it bypasses this problem at all. Either of these things is a way to force the .Rmd document to be knit from scratch again, and so it no longer tries to use the cached .html file.

The glass half-empty side of this bug is that it exists at all and that you, the app author, have to deal with it. The glass half-full side is that dealing with it is very easy, once you know it: just delete the old .html file.

## The hint of a better explanation
This is an issue that can actually affect any `runtime: shiny_prerendered` .Rmd document. The root source of this problem is in the `rmarkdown` package and it is documented at https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1278. Once that issue is addressed, this type of problem should disappear completely in future releases. And I'll close this issue here too.

The particular problem you saw above (involving 'highlightjs-1.1') was monkey patched in rmarkdown 1.8.9 (rmakrdown 1.9 is now avaibale on CRAN): https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/commit/d3331691947add59b20c65459e1f3a0b3f15173e. However, this only "takes off" after the .html file is regenerated. The easiest way to do this is simply to delete the old .html file and re-run the .Rmd tutorial from scratch.

There's a chance there will be other dependency changes causing similar errors before this issue is fully addressed on the `rmarkdown` side. Regenerating the .html file from scratch should resolve the issue. If not, please comment below or open a new issue.

title: how can add images in learnr
Adding hyperlinks to incorrect message
description:
It's possible to add a hyperlink to the message displayed when an incorrect choice is selected for a multiple choice question, e.g.

```r
question("What number is the letter A in the alphabet?",
         answer("8", message = "See [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_alphabet) and try again."),
         answer("14"),
         answer("1", correct = TRUE),
         answer("23"), 
         allow_retry = TRUE
         )
```

However in most cases I'd like to display the same incorrect message for all wrong answers, so would like to be able to do something like the following.

```r
question("What number is the letter A in the alphabet?",
         answer("8"),
         answer("14"),
         answer("1", correct = TRUE),
         answer("23"), 
         incorrect = "See [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_alphabet) and try again.",
         allow_retry = TRUE
         )
```

This doesn't give an error however the hyperlink does not work. I think it would be a nice feature to add. The current alternative is the following, which requires repeating the message for each option.

```r
question("What number is the letter A in the alphabet?",
         answer("8", message = "See [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_alphabet) and try again."),
         answer("14", message = "See [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_alphabet) and try again."),
         answer("1", correct = TRUE),
         answer("23", message = "See [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_alphabet) and try again."), 
         allow_retry = TRUE
         )
```

title: custom css not honored?
description:
No matter what I change in a custom css in `learn::tutorial()`, it does not has any effect on the resulting html.

```YAML
learnr::tutorial:
    theme: simplex
    df_print: tibble
    progressive: false
    css: "rstudio-theme.css"
```

Here is the pandoc call (v2.0.1). Also tried it with RStudio's pandoc.

```
/usr/local/bin/pandoc +RTS -K512m -RTS raster_exercise_learnr.utf8.md --to html 
--from markdown+autolink_bare_uris+ascii_identifiers+tex_math_single_backslash 
--output raster_exercise_learnr.html --email-obfuscation none --section-divs 
--template /usr/local/lib/R/3.4/site-library/learnr/rmarkdown/templates/tutorial/resources/tutorial-format.htm 
--no-highlight --css rstudio-theme.css --variable progressive=false 
--variable allow-skip=false --id-prefix section- --variable 'theme:simplex' 
--mathjax 
--variable 'mathjax-url:https://mathjax.rstudio.com/latest/MathJax.js?config=TeX-AMS-MML_HTMLorMML'
```

When I inspect the resulting html file in my browser, only the css from the `theme` is shown and applied. 
As a reprex I used the [`rstudio-theme.css`](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/blob/master/inst/rmarkdown/templates/tutorial/resources/rstudio-theme.css) and hoped that it overrides the style of the chosen theme. This should work if I'm not mistaken. (This is only for reprex reasons, I know one can set the rstudio theme with `theme: <theme>`.

The custom css is linked  (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="rstudio-theme.css">`) but has no effect.

description:

title: exercise = TRUE displays solution button; exercise = T does not
description:

````
---
title: "Test"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

## Sample Problems

Find $2 + 2$.

```{r e1, exercise = TRUE}

```

```{r e1-solution}
2 + 2
```

Now find $3 \times 3$.

```{r e2, exercise = T}

```

```{r e2-solution}
3 * 3
```
<!-- no button, and the code above is rendered -->
````

I am using Firefox version 54 on Debian version 8.8. Being implemented in JavaScript, there's not much hope of avoiding this.

title: Ability to parse solution-code or check-code as an actual numeric or character, not the code to get it
description:
Suppose I want the user to tell me, and I don't care how she gets it, what is "the mean of the 3rd column" in a given `data.frame`:

    What is the mean of the 3rd column in df?
    ```{r q1, exercise = TRUE, exercise.eval = FALSE, exercise.lines = 1}

    ```

    ```{r q1-solution}
    mean(df[, 3])
    ```

    ```{r q1-check}
    mean(df[, 3])
    ```

In this scenario, the only correct answer is `mean(df[, 3])`, but there are many ways to get there, and I want the correct answer to be simply the actual number, say `3.5`.

Currently I can't do that without writing in the solution explicitly `3.5`, and this becomes an issue say if the data.frame `df` (or any other object I'm asking about) was created dynamically, e.g. by sampling, and I can't hard-code it.

title: Responsive images
description:
Not entirely sure this is how it should work but using markdown to include images doesn't add the bootstrap `img-responsive` class.

Not responsive:
`![my_image](images/myimage.png)`

Responsive:
`img(src = "images/myimage.png", alt="my_image", class="img-responsive")`

title: Trouble if you deploy with an existing connection open in the browser
description:
If you republish a tutorial while an existing connection to the tutorial is open in the browser, the new tutorial will appear not to work. Specifically, the progress indicators and continue buttons will not function. If you close the previously open connection to the tutorial, the new connection will immediately restore status and begin to work. In either case, if you close all connections and then re-open the tutorial, it will work. In other words, the deployment is ultimately successful but will seem buggy if you do not probe deeper.

I'm not sure that this is an issue that requires any development work, but it took me quite a long time to figure out what was going on - so I wanted to get the word out.

I noticed this phenomenon on Google Chrome and have reproduced it several times. It may be limited to tutorials that use progressive reveal.

title: RStudio feature request for creating tutorials
description: When creating tutorials, it would be nice if either the "run all previous code" button or the "run this chunk" button (or some additional button) would only run the setup chunks that will be run before the exercise is launched.  (Perhaps it could also clear objects from the workspace first, too.)  That would make it easier to ensure that the exercise code will execute properly when the tutorial is run.

title: Data files on shiny server
description:
When running tutorials locally one can set the path to whatever directory in the local machine and then read files from that directory.

However, when one publishes the tutorial on a server, it is not clear how to access the data files (external sources) that have been uploaded together with the Rmd tutorial file. The default current directory when calling `getwd()` in an exercise chunk is not the directory of the tutorial Rmd.

Please provide a solution so that either the working directory is by default the directory containing the Rmd tutorial file or another solution to call the data files from inside the chunks without having to input the whole absolute path to the data.

title: delay between when a tutorial loads and when it advances to the saved state.
description:
I think this is an unanticipated interaction with progressive reveal.

@garrettgman

https://tutorials.shinyapps.io/04-programming-basics/
https://tutorials.shinyapps.io/04-programming-basics-alt/

[setup-issues.Rmd.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/files/1079380/setup-issues.Rmd.txt)

title: undesired feature: setup chunks always hidden
description:
It appears that if an R chunk is used with `exercise.setup`, then there is no way to make it visible.  But I would like to have some code that is visible to the user, but not editable, followed by an exercise chunk where they use that code.

In my particular use case, I want to define a function and let the user experiment with different argument values, but I don't want them to be able to break the function itself.

`echo = TRUE` seems not to work on these chunks.

title: Progressive Reveal feature not working on shinyapp servers
description:
Running my Rmd locally works fine, and all exercises reveal after the previous ones are completed by a user. However, when running on a server, it seems like R doesn't recognize that the answers have been submitted/ the code has been run, and I get the following error:

"You must complete the exercise in this section before continuing."

when clicking on a Continue button. 

(I am using checkr package in the tutorial).

title: It would be nice if package tutorials could be listed like vignettes in packages documentation.
description: Is this controlled by core R or is it possible to add tutorials to the "User guides, package vignettes and other documentation." that shows up when you click on a package name in the Packages tab.

title: Should it possible to get a solution and a hint for the same code chunk?
description: This seems to not work at the moment.  I only see the hint if there is a hint and a solution.

title: footnotes in tutorials
description: Is it possible to have footnotes show up only in the topic where they are created instead of at the bottom of the page in every topic?  It is distracting to have the footnote information show up before the footnote marker has appeared.

title: HTML table output not rendering
description:
When using progressive rendering (`progressive: true`), and when I have an HTML table output produced from code such as the following in a future section,

```{r}
mtcars
```

the HTML tables often do not show up and the user is required to refresh the page.  Also, the refresh brings the user back to the top of the tutorial requiring them to scroll down to where they left off.

As an example, if you run the following:

`devtools::install_github("bradleyboehmke/learningAnalytics")`
`learningAnalytics::get_tutorial("Linear Regression")`

and work through the first few exercises until you get to the __Assessing Coefficients__ section you will notice a blank table after the `tidy(model1)` line.  If you refresh it will display properly.

I taught a short course of 18 and all 18 had this same problem throughout the tutorials.  However, note that this was the *only* complaint as everyone loved this integrated learning approach.  Definite kudos to a great package!

title: Browser navigation in tutorials
description:
It would be nice to be able to get completely out of a tutorial more easily.  As is, there are multiple ways to navigate within the pages of a tutorial, but no good way to get back to the page one was on before starting the tutorial.

Is there a way to do that given the current set-up?  I'm imagining that one might publish a page with links to several tutorials, and someone might get part way into one of the tutorials and like to get back to the referring page.

title: Is there any way for end user to control size of plots?
description:
This one might be trickier.

The creator of a tutorial can use `fig.height` to allocate space.  But the amount of space desired might depend on the plot the user makes.  Is there any way to make that something the user of the tutorial can adjust?

title: Remove duplicate display of second level header?
description:
Each second level header appears once in the sidebar and once in the content, where it is often followed immediately by a third level header (if you do not follow it with a third level header, the tutorial will reveal the first two sub-sections at once when progressive reveal  is turned on).

I think this scheme is sub-optimal because I sometimes need to come up with a meaningless third level header to make the progressive reveal work right. The three levels of text that result also look a bit disorienting.

Is it possible to remove the duplicate header (see below)? If an author wants the section title to appear at the top of the section, he or she could repeat it in a third level header.

![untitled 001](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/85014/26695067/767bb1be-46d7-11e7-882c-9179f2f70bbb.png)

````
---
title: "Exploratory Data Analysis"
output: 
  learnr::tutorial:
    progressive: true
    allow_skip: true
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
```

## Welcome to EDA

## What is EDA?

### Well what is it?

EDA is Exploratory Data Analysis, everyone's favorite tool. 

### The history of EDA

EDA was popularized by John Tukey.

## The EDA mindset

````

title: Add button to hide or delete R output?
description: I'm thinking of something like the double ^ or X in RStudio's notebook. In the case of double ^, we might like double V to bring the output back (presumably without rerunning it).

title: Explicit support for "fill in the blank" code templates?
description:
Just thinking aloud here...

One useful way to teach code paradigms is to provide a template and have learners "fill in the blanks".  @dtkaplan has been using a convention like 

```r
xyplot ( __y__ ~ __x__, data = __dataset__ )
```
to indicate the blanks.

Might there eventually be a formal way of doing this?  Here are some ideas about how it could work.  (We probably need to think a bit more about what the desired behavior would be).

  1. Display things like `__y__` in a different color and or font
  2. Convert things like `__y__` into fill-in boxes -- and perhaps not allow other code editing
  3. Blank-specific hints on hover (like tooltips)?
 
Some of these sorts of things probably mean work since they require parsing the R code to find the non-R mark-up.

title: Can hints be turned back off?
description: The hint function is nice, but I think it would be nice if the hint button functioned as a toggle so the hint can be rehidden if desired.

title: Creating variables in the startup chunk
description: It appears that one must explicitly make assignments into the global environment using `<<-` or `assign()` with `pos = globalenv()` in order for them to be available in subsequent exercise blocks.  Is this correct?  Intended?

title: Code Reset button?
description: It would be nice if users could reset the code in an individual code block back to the state before they began edits without having to restart the entire tutorial.  Would this be easy to add?

title: Support for other languages in exercise chunks?
description:
Given `rmarkdown` and `knitr` support for other languages, would it be possible for `learnr` to support other languages in exercise chunks? It would be useful to build tutorials for other languages, and/or for pipelines that span multiple languages.

Thank you.

title: multiple set up chunks needed in long tutorial
description:
First of all, I have to say thank you to you all for making this package. I teach 1.5-hour- to 3-day-long seminars on various topics in R and Stata and I think learnr made for the best participant experience of any session I've ever done. I am happy to report that my learnr tutorial worked flawlessly on 30 computers running various versions of RStudio and multiple operating systems.

I do want to report an issue though for you to check out. You can view my repository [here](https://github.com/strategicdataproject/dataviz-r). Sorry for lack of short reproducible example.

I need only one set up chunk where I load a short data frame. However, to get the document to run, for some reason I had to periodically repeat the same set up chunk with a new name. You'll see this in my document where I have loadData, loadData2, loadData3, etc. If you replace, for example, loadData2 with loadData as the set up chunk, the document will not run even though they are exactly the same chunk of code. I forget the exact error message. I can reproduce if you don't have time to look at my repo.

title: Collaborative simultaneous editing
description:
It would be nice in a classroom setting to be able to edit the contents of an exercise chunk in collaboration with other people. The isolation of chunks from each other would prevent this from becoming too complex for the users. Maybe this could be setup via the URL query string, e.g.

`https://dtkaplan.shinyapps.io/Workshop_wrangling?share=d4a78`

The instructor, or whoever, could post the URL on, say, the course syllabus for that day. I'm imagining that this behavior would be tied to the use of a particular server, e.g. shinyapps.io or rcloud.

title: Code in global setup chunk cannot be referenced under Windows
description:
It seems that code added to the global setup chunk cannot be referenced under Windows.
Here is a small reproducible example:

    ---
    title: "Tutorial"
    output: learnr::tutorial
    runtime: shiny_prerendered
    ---

    ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
    library(learnr)
    nycflights <- nycflights13::flights
    ```

title: Progressive reveal does not yet function as an educational aid.
description:
E-learning/Multimedia Learning theory suggests that progressive reveal will enhance student learning when it:

1. divides large segments of information into digestible chunks
2. gives students time to reflect on what they've learned before moving on
3. places the student in control of when to move on
4. guides student attention to the small chunk of information that they should focus on
5. (implied: not distract or confuse the student)

I think we need to make several changes to meet these goals (all but one mentioned in other issues):

1. Have reveal occur at every third level header as well as *after every exercise* (not yet implemented). This is because each exercise/feedback combination forms an important chunk of information that requires the student to reflect and conserve attention.

2. Add explicit "Go On" buttons everywhere a hidden section occurs #26, #25. This makes it obvious that a progressive reveal system exists and it provides an effortless way for the student to use it.

3. Have new sections fade or dissolve in to attract the student's attention. Instant change disorients, moderate change attracts attention, very slow change becomes subliminal. #27

title: Fade in for progressive reveal
description:
Can new section dissolve (quickly) into view instead of appearing all at once? This would:

1. Better draw the student's attention to the new section
2. Reduce the disorientation of a section appearing when the student may not expect it

(This last point may be due to the connection between exercise completion and reveals: the student submits their code, which primes them to see a piece of feedback. Then, an entire new section appears, burying the feedback. #25, #26)

description:
It would be useful to have a way to turn progressive reveal off for individual sub-sections, e.g.

````
### A not-hidden sub-section {data-progressive = FALSE}
````

In this case, the sub-section would appear when the previous sub-section appears (which might itself be triggered by a progressive reveal).

title: Progressive reveal does not provide a cue that a hidden section follows.
description: When progressive reveal is on, there is no indication to the reader that a tutorial contains hidden sections to unlock. For example, there is a hidden section waiting to be revealed here (code below): A user can miss the hidden sub-section by using the TOC to navigate past them. Related to #25 because a user will always miss sub-sections if the current sub-section does not contain an exercise (the method for revealing sub-sections). They will also miss hidden sections when they choose not to do an exercise. Both issues can be resolved by separating progressive reveal from exercise completion and tying it to a "Go On" button that appears whenever a hidden section follows. ```` --- title: "Demo Tutorial" output: tutor::tutorial: progressive: true runtime: shiny_prerendered --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} library(tutor) checker <- function(label, user_code, check_code, envir_result, evaluate_result, ...) { list(message = "Good Job!", correct = TRUE, location = "append") } tutor_options(exercise.checker = checker) ``` ## Welcome ### Visible sub-section This sub-section is visible. It contains a boring exercise that you choose not to do. Notice that there is no "Next Topic" button. ```{r one, exercise = TRUE} ``` ```{r one-check} "foo" ``` ### Hidden sub-section This sub-section is hidden. You do not know that it exists. ## Second Task Once "finished" above, you can navigate here with the TOC. ````

title: Cannot progressively reveal sub-sections that follow a sub-section that has no exercises
description:
Progressive reveal seems to rely on exercise completion to trigger reveals. As a result, you cannot reveal the next sub-section if the current sub-section does not contain an exercise. Related to #26.

To see this in action, launch the tutorial below and then compare the behavior of "First Section" to the behavior of "Second Section".

````
---
title: "Demo Tutorial"
output: 
  tutor::tutorial:
    progressive: true
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tutor)
checker <- function(label, user_code, check_code, envir_result, evaluate_result, ...) {
  list(message = "Good Job!", correct = TRUE, location = "append")
}
tutor_options(exercise.checker = checker)
```

## Welcome

This is the Welcome section. It has an exercise to ensure that the TOC appears. Click "Submit Code" to move on.

```{r one, exercise = TRUE}

```

```{r one-check}
"foo"
```

## First task

### Visible sub-section

description:
If possible, I would like to create tutorials that teach students how to use R Markdown. To do this interactively, I would need a second type of interactive exercise block: a block whose content is assumed to be an R Markdown document and whose display comes with a "Knit Document" button.

Is it technically feasible to create such a block?

title: Obtaining assessment data (pass/fail/trials)
description:
Glancing over the documentation, [the event recorders](https://rstudio.github.io/tutor/publishing.html#recording_events) only supply data presently for submission, error, or hint. Is there any way to obtain more granularity on this such that the outcome of the submission could be discriminate as being either correct or incorrect?

If so, then potentially the responses could be aggregated in a database and used to effectively assess students under a [Shiny Pro Server setup](https://rstudio.github.io/tutor/publishing.html#shiny_server) assuming login was required. In essence, this has the potential to be the nbgrader feature of the Jupyter notebooks but for _R_.

title: Wrong event-recorder entry for questions when random order is TRUE.
description: For multiple-choice questions, the `data` argument passed to the function assigned to `tutor.event_recorder` can have the wrong value in the `answers:` field when `random_answer_order = TRUE`. Instead of giving the answer text that corresponds to the selected option in the HTML display, the text is pulled out from the original order given in the `question()` function that set up the possible answers. In other words, randomization is done correctly so far as the display and the evaluation of correctness, but the event recorder doesn't seem to know about the randomization.

title: File names can't start with non-alpha
description:
A tutor Rmd file whose name begins with a non-alphabetic character, e.g. `05-collection.Rmd`, will run only if there are no graphics chunks in the document. This behavior is inherited from `shiny::add_resource_path`. Files without graphics chunks work find, even with names starting with a numeral.

The obvious quick fix is not to start tutor Rmd file names with a non-alphabetic character.  (This is a moral conflict with the naming style encouraged by `bookdown`, but not a technical conflict.) Still, the start-with-alphabetical-character-if-graphics-chunk is perhaps unnecessarily obscure.

title: Feature request: Hints with markdown formatting
description: Might there be a `markdown = TRUE` chunk option added so that hints will be displayed in formatted text rather than in monospace? Often, I would like to give a hint that is narrative, rather than code based.

title: Feature request: pre-checking of code
description:
The student's submitted code is evaluated *before* handing it off to the checker function. This makes sense, but when the evaluation fails, the student gets feedback from R rather than from the checking code. 

Might it be arranged to send the code to a pre-evaluation checking chunk. Then the checking system can have at it before R. Feedback messages would be returned in the usual way. Only if the feedback is passing, should the code be evaluated. Then the evaluated code can be sent again to the checking system. Since the checking system knows specifically what the code should look like, it can perhaps identify problems that don't produce helpful errors from R.
